history.sg_progress: Redeployment of resources within a budget section and within non-post objects of expenditure are permitted under the current regulatory framework. Adjustments to the plan are also permitted, in accordance with rule 106.2 (b) of the Regulations and Rules Governing Programme Planning, the Programme Aspects of the Budget, the Monitoring of Implementation and the Methods of Evaluation, which gives programme managers the discretion to reformulate their plans, provided that it is in pursuance of the objective and strategy of the subprogramme. Redeployments do not require prior General Assembly approval and, pursuant to paragraph 29 of resolution 77/267, the primary consideration in determining the resource requirements is the effective delivery of mandates. The Administration continues to monitor budget implementation in accordance with the current regulatory framework. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.

history.entities_raw: Department of Management Strategy, Policy and Compliance
history.sg_progress: In line with legislative recommendations to follow the presentation of peacekeeping budgets, there is no reporting done using the furniture and equipment class of expenditure for special political missions. Information on budget performance is provided in the peacekeeping budget format. For material differences between the budget appropriation and actual expenditure amounts, a full variance analysis is prepared as part of the financial performance report on the programme budget, which, for 2023, was provided in the annexes for the ICT expenditure incurred in 2023 by special political missions. More detailed explanations are provided in the supplementary information provided to the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions and the Fifth Committee, which includes justification for additional acquisition of ICT equipment owing to operational needs and after considering the current condition of the existing equipment. The Administration considers the recommendation implemented and had requested its closure on the basis of the enhancement of the supplementary of the 2024 proposed budget for special political missions that included an additional annex providing financial performance for 2022, with variance analysis and justification for any material difference between appropriation and expenditure at the budget class level for each mission. It should also be noted that the special political mission budgets were presented to the legislative bodies in the peacekeeping format (using peacekeeping budget classes), and there was no furniture and equipment class in that format. In addition, the Administration added to the allotment advice to special political missions the relevant reminders, but the Board did not agree to close the recommendation. The Administration looks forward to re-engaging with the Board during its next audit visit to define clear and achievable implementation criteria.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration continue to monitor budget implementation, in particular for those entities with continuous overexpenditure on furniture and equipment, in accordance with the parameters established by the General Assembly.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented. The existence of variances against the approved budget is not a valid reason for keeping this recommendation open. Heads of entities are allowed to redeploy funds within their allotment in order to effectively implement entities’ mandates and respond to operational requirements. Variances against the approved budget that arise during budget implementation and the related justifications are reported to the General Assembly in the supplementary information, ensuring transparency. Therefore, the Administration respectfully requests the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that variances against the approved budget that arise during budget implementation and the related justifications are reported to the General Assembly in the supplementary information, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
